args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks in production (18% error rate) following its deploy. Rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback completed and verified; service is now running v2.3.0. Investigating team should root-cause v2.3.1 before re-deploy.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary:

**Rollback completed:**
- v2.3.1 was running unhealthy in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.
- v2.3.0 was the most recent release healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc was only staging, so it didn't qualify).
- Rolled back all three production regions to **v2.3.0** — service is now healthy with error rate back down to 0.2%.

**Incident opened:**
- **INC-0001** (SEV2, checkout-api) — paged the on-call engineer, describing the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback to v2.3.0, and the follow-up to root-cause v2.3.1 before re-deploy.

transcript.content: I'll start by checking the deployment history to find the most recent healthy release, and check the current service status.

transcript.reasoning_content: Current: v2.3.1 unhealthy. Most recent healthy release in production: v2.3.0. Rollback doesn't need approval (deploying a never-healthy version does; rollback to previously healthy one is fine).

transcript.content: The rollback completed successfully. Let me verify health and open the incident.
